text: Translation Assistant 是面向 DSH Web 的 AI 翻译与校对插件。它在 Harness Host 注册浏览器工作台和 translation_assistant Agent 工具，并通过模型路由处理翻译请求。用户可以翻译文本、文件和工作区文档，按句子或段落处理，读取截图文字，附加术语与文风规范，查看评分评语并据此重写，还可查看本地历史与版本。适合需要在 DSH 中翻译和审校文档的用户。需要 Harness 提供可用的默认模型，或在插件配置中指定模型路由。

Translation Assistant adds AI translation and review to the DSH web client. Its Host serves a browser workspace and an Agent tool for translating, rewriting, and scoring. It handles sentences, documents, files, glossary notes, and style rules. A Harness model route is required.
想在 DSH 里把一段外文快速翻成中文。
有没有办法把整份文档翻译，同时保留段落对应关系？
我想导入截图识别文字，再把识别结果翻译出来。
让翻译时自动参考我项目里的术语表和风格说明。
译文读起来不自然，能按我的意见让模型重写吗？
我想给译文打分并查看哪些地方需要改进。
I need to translate a folder of project files and review the results in one place.
Can I ask my chat assistant to translate or score a passage for me?
Translation Assistant 的分段翻译：按句子或段落切分文本，并限制并发处理，返回与输入顺序对应的译文。
Translation Assistant 的工作区翻译：浏览项目文件并打开支持的文档，翻译后可将文本结果写回工作区文件。
Translation Assistant 的翻译评审：为单句、段落或全文生成 0–100 分数和简短评语，可用于检查现有译文。
Translation Assistant 的 Agent 工具：聊天助手可调用 translate、retranslate、score 和 score_document 操作处理文本。

dsh-translation-assistant README · Translation Assistant：A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns translation into an AI workflow: the model drafts, you direct. Text, files, screenshots, and whole folders are translated by AI; your glossary and style rules ride along on every request; every score and comment you leave becomes the instruction for an AI rewrite; and each pass keeps a rollback point. The job shifts from typing translations to judging them.

[中文](README.zh.md)

**What the AI workflow changes**

dsh-translation-assistant README · Translation Assistant：| Before | With Translation Assistant |
| --- | --- |
| Type every segment; look terms up as you go | AI drafts the full text in one pass — a `.translation-spec/` glossary and style rules are attached to every request automatically |
| Mark problems, then retype the fixes | Score a segment and write one comment; `Apply suggestion` turns both into the rewrite instruction for that segment |
| Copy-paste files into a translator tab, one at a time | Point the workspace at a folder: batch translation walks every pending file and writes the results back to disk while you review what has landed |
| One model has to do everything | One model translates, another reviews: the draft comes from a fast model, and a stronger one scores it and rewrites from its own comments |
| Switch windows to translate a snippet from chat | The same engine is an Agent tool — the assistant translates and reviews inside the conversation |

dsh-translation-assistant README · Translation Assistant：- **AI at every step** — drafting, retranslating with your prompt, scoring, rewriting from your comments, and reading text out of screenshots are all model calls; the plugin orchestrates them into one loop.
- **Review instead of retyping** — the side-by-side view shows the draft; you touch only the segments that need it, and AI applies your notes to the rest.
- **A two-model loop** — one model produces the draft, another scores it, and every score becomes a rewrite instruction; each pass leaves a revision you can roll back to.
- **Guidelines travel with every request** — the workspace's `.translation-spec/` folder holds glossary and style documents; translation, retranslation, scoring, and batch jobs all include them.
- **Not just a page, an Agent tool** — the engine answers `translation_assistant` calls (`translate | retranslate | score | score_document`) inside chat.
- **Local first** — history and edits never leave the browser; bring your own models.

dsh-translation-assistant README · Install：One line from a terminal:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-translation-assistant
```

Or from the GUI: **Plugins → Add plugin**, enter `dsh-translation-assistant`, press **Install**, then **Enable now**.

Local checkout, Git address, manual registry, and upgrading or uninstalling: [docs/install.md](docs/install.md).

dsh-translation-assistant README · Translate：- `By paragraph` or `By sentence`, both returned in one pass; speed-first mode runs chunks concurrently and shows a `Translating n/m` counter.
- Three AI translation modes, picked on the new-translation form and in the full-text card. When a response does not match the chosen protocol, the pass falls back to batching without raising an error.

dsh-translation-assistant README · Translate：| Mode | Trait | Best for |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Coherence first | One request for the full text, the fullest context | Essays, reports — the default |
  | Alignment first | JSON-array protocol, the strongest paragraph alignment | Glossaries, subtitles, strict side-by-side layouts |
  | Speed first | Chunked three-way concurrency, fastest on long texts | Time-boxed bulk jobs |

dsh-translation-assistant README · Translate：- **Files** — drop or pick `.txt`, `.md`, `.log`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.docx` (Word files are unpacked in the browser; the original never leaves the machine).
- **Images** — paste or pick a screenshot; AI transcribes it, then translates.

dsh-translation-assistant README · Workspace：- Workspaces are the projects you already added in Harness: a picker at the top of the drawer lists every project folder, selection switches instantly, and the last one is remembered. Reads and writes stay confined to the selected project; the drawer never covers what you are proofreading.
- When the host does not expose the project list (e.g. `dsh web`), a collapsible manual path entry serves as the fallback; an outdated Host side (404) points to a Harness restart.
- The tree folds by folder; clicking a file name opens it — untranslated files start translating immediately, translated ones reopen for proofreading.
- Output goes to a `translated/` subfolder (default), a suffixed sibling copy, over the original, or stays on the page only without touching disk; `.docx` translations always save as `.md`. Proofread edits can auto-save or wait for the save button.
- `Translate all` walks the pending files in order and saves each result; a stop ends the run after the file in flight. While workspace content is open, the workspace button shows the project's name.
- A `.translation-spec/` folder in the workspace holds guideline documents (`glossar

dsh-translation-assistant README · Review and refine：- Source and translation sit side by side; every segment is editable, and edits re-join sentences and paragraphs correctly.
- `AI retranslate` redoes one segment; `Retranslate with prompt` adds an instruction such as "more colloquial". Both follow the translation mode and leave one revision per pass.
- Scores are on demand only: score a segment, the current view, or the whole document, then reveal them from the toolbar. `Apply suggestion` sends a score and its comment back as the instruction for a fresh AI pass; `Apply all` rewrites every scored segment three at a time.
- A `Stop` button sits beside every running pass; in-flight requests are cancelled, and rewrites that already landed are kept.

dsh-translation-assistant README · Keep track：- On-device history — up to 200 documents with search, pinning, and two-click deletion.
- Revisions — up to 100 snapshots per document; the drawer shows how far each one differs from the current text, and restoring is undoable.

dsh-translation-assistant README · Integrate：- The header picker groups models by provider; `Follow default` tracks the profile, any other entry pins the route for translation, retranslation, scoring, and OCR — so a cheap model can draft while a stronger one reviews. Outside providers register through Harness settings — a worked example in [docs/bilibili-index-translate.md](docs/bilibili-index-translate.md).
- The same engine is exposed as a `translation_assistant` Agent tool (`translate | retranslate | score | score_document`), so the chat assistant can translate or review text as part of its own workflow.

dsh-translation-assistant README · Use cases：**One model drafts, another reviews.** Translate with a fast model, then switch to your strongest model and run `Score all`, then `Apply all`. Each rewrite carries the score and its comment as the instruction, so the strong model fixes exactly what it criticised — and every pass leaves a revision, so comparing and rolling back is one click.

dsh-translation-assistant README · Use cases：**A whole folder under your rules.** Drop a `glossary.md` and a `style.md` into `.translation-spec/`, point the workspace at the project, and press `Translate all`: every file is translated with the same guidelines attached and written back to disk, and you review the results side by side afterwards.

dsh-translation-assistant README · Use cases：**A whole document, end to end.** Drop a `.docx`, `.md`, or `.html` file: it is translated in one request, and `Download translation` writes the result back in the same shape with the paragraph structure intact.

dsh-translation-assistant README · How it works：`host/index.js` registers a same-origin `/dsh-translation/api` route and the Agent tool, `host/engine.js` does the model work (no Harness imports), and `client.js` is the page. POSTs are origin-checked and capped at 24 MiB, and every request can pin a `route: { provider, model }`.

Endpoints, configuration fields, on-device storage, the full limits, and maintainer notes: [docs/reference.md](docs/reference.md).

dsh-translation-assistant README · Privacy：History, edits, and preferences never leave the browser; only the text being translated, retranslated, scored, or read from an image is sent to the model route. Clearing site data for the Harness origin erases the history — there is no server-side copy.

dsh-translation-assistant README · Development and verification：```bash
node --test 'test/*.test.mjs'
```

The repository doubles as the installed bundle: `client.js` hot-swaps into the open page, Host changes need a Harness restart. The screenshots in `docs/screenshots/` are real renders against mocked data — retake them after layout changes.
dsh-translation-assistant README · Troubleshooting：See [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md).
